transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I don’t feel any interest in the things I used to love—my art, my garden, even time with my family just feels flat. I just don't seem to care about the things that used to define my days, and everything feels completely empty.
How long have you been feeling this way, and was there a specific event or time when you noticed your interest in these activities started to decrease?

These feelings have been building for a little over two years now. It really started about two and a half years ago when my kids became more independent and my husband began traveling constantly for work, leaving me alone at home. I tried to keep myself busy with my garden and art at first, but gradually I just withdrew from everything.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns over the past two and a half years, alongside the loss of interest in your usual activities?

Yes, my appetite is all over the place—some weeks I skip meals without noticing, and other weeks I'm mindlessly snacking at night, which has made my clothes fit differently. As for sleep, during my high-energy phases I can get by on just three or four hours, spending the night on my laptop or rearranging things and still waking up buzzing. It has been incredibly inconsistent.

You mentioned having high-energy phases where you can get by on less sleep and are very active, but also periods where everything feels empty. Can you tell me more about these high-energy phases, such as how often they occur and how they make you feel compared to your low-energy or empty feeling phases?

During those high-energy times, which have been coming and going for about a year and eight months, I feel wired, giddy, and so confident that I'll rush around starting a dozen projects, though I also get easily annoyed. It's a huge contrast to the low phases, which feel heavy and gray like a crash where everything is pointless, and those have lasted about seven months in total.

Can you estimate how many days or weeks these high-energy phases typically last, and do they always transition into the low-energy or empty feeling phases, or can they resolve on their own without a noticeable crash?

I'm really not sure about the exact number of days or weeks they last, or exactly how they transition. I just know these phases have been coming and going for about a year and eight months, and I often end up crashing or feeling completely exhausted afterward. I haven't really tracked the precise timing or patterns of how they shift.

Can you describe if there are any distinct periods where you feel extremely happy, irritable, or overly confident, and if so, how these periods relate to your energy levels and interest in activities?

Yes, during those "up" periods I feel suddenly wired, giddy, or easily irritated, and I talk very fast. My energy levels skyrocket and I get overly confident, convinced I'm going to create this massive art-therapy program, so I rush around starting projects and signing up for workshops. But I eventually crash, leaving everything half-finished and feeling exhausted.
Do you experience these mood swings or energy shifts without any apparent reason or trigger, or are they usually preceded by specific events or circumstances?

They really seem to happen out of nowhere without any clear trigger. On my low days, I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling for no clear reason, and during the high-energy times, I suddenly feel wired, giddy, and irritable for no good reason at all.

Can you clarify if your high-energy phases and low-energy phases meet the criteria of lasting at least two weeks for the depressive phases and at least one week but less than two weeks for the hypomanic phases, or if they vary significantly in duration?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days or weeks that each individual stretch lasts. I just know that these high and low phases have been coming and going over the past year or two, and it's hard for me to keep track of the precise timing.

Can you try to estimate or recall if there have been periods where you felt extremely low or depressed for at least two weeks, and separately, periods where you felt unusually high or irritable for at least four consecutive days?

Yes, I've definitely experienced both of those. The low, depressed stretches where I feel heavy and empty usually drag on for weeks at a time, adding up to about seven months overall. On the other hand, those high-energy, irritable phases have been coming and going for about a year and eight months, lasting for days at a time where I feel wired, talk fast, and barely sleep.

Can you confirm whether your high-energy, irritable phases, where you feel wired and talk fast, have ever lasted at least four consecutive days, but less than a week, without any significant depressive episodes in between?

I'm not really sure about the exact number of days those high-energy phases last, as I haven't tracked them that closely. They definitely come and go, but I can't pin down the precise duration of each stretch.

Can you think of any instance where your high-energy, irritable phase lasted at least four consecutive days but less than a week, and if so, did it significantly impact your daily life or relationships?

I'm not sure about the exact number of days because my sense of time gets really blurry when I'm in those phases. However, they definitely happen and make me feel incredibly wired and irritable, which has caused a lot of strain on my family due to arguments and all the half-finished projects I leave around the house.

Can you recall any specific instance where you felt extremely high or irritable for at least four consecutive days but less than a week, without a significant depressive episode immediately following it, and how that affected your daily functioning and relationships?

I'm still not sure of the exact day count for those stretches, and while I do crash into a depression sometimes, other times my mood just levels out. But during those high phases, it definitely affects my life—I get very annoyed with my family, leave half-finished projects everywhere, and let things like bills pile up.

Can you recall any specific instance where you felt extremely high or irritable for at least four consecutive days, and if so, did you experience any depressive symptoms immediately after, or did your mood return to normal?

Yes, those high, wired, and irritable phases definitely last for days at a time, often going on for a week or more. When they finally end, I don't just go back to normal; instead, I usually crash hard into those heavy, flat, and empty feelings where I feel completely drained and guilty.

Can you confirm if there has ever been a period where you felt extremely high or irritable for at least four consecutive days but less than a week, without immediately transitioning into a depressive episode?

I'm really not sure about the exact number of days those high periods last or how they transition, as I haven't tracked them that closely. It's hard for me to say if there was a time they lasted less than a week without a crash afterward.

Can you think of any instance where you had a period of feeling extremely high or irritable that lasted at least four consecutive days but less than a week, and if so, did it end with a return to a normal mood or immediately transition into a depressive episode?

I definitely experience those high, wired, and irritable periods where I run around starting all kinds of projects, and I always end up crashing afterward. However, I'm just not sure of the exact number of days they last, like if it's exactly four to six days, or whether my mood returns to normal first versus sliding straight into a depressed state. It all feels a bit blurry when I try to look back on it.

Can you try to recall any specific instance where you felt extremely high or irritable for at least four consecutive days but less than a week, and if so, did you experience any noticeable decrease in functioning or require any intervention during or after those episodes?

I definitely experience those high and irritable periods, but I'm really not sure exactly how many days they last at a time. During those times, I do notice that I end up leaving a lot of projects half-done and letting household tasks pile up. I've just never tracked the specific duration closely enough to know how long they go on.

Can you try to estimate or recall if there was ever a time when you felt extremely high or irritable for at least four consecutive days but less than a week, without a significant depressive episode immediately following it, and how that period affected your daily functioning?

I really can't recall the exact duration of those high or irritable periods, so I don't know if they have ever lasted exactly four to six days. I just know that I do experience these wired, high-energy phases on and off, which always lead to me starting a lot of projects and leaving them completely unfinished.

These high, wired phases have been coming and going for about a year and eight months, and during them, I feel buzzed, talk fast, and sleep only three or four hours. I don't know the exact number of days they last, but they definitely go on for days at a time where I start a dozen projects and make big plans. It really strains my relationship with my family because I get so easily annoyed, and when I eventually crash, I feel so embarrassed by the mess of unfinished things I've left behind.

Can you recall any instance where you had a distinct period of feeling extremely high or irritable that lasted at least four consecutive days but less than two weeks, and if so, did you experience any significant impairment in social or occupational functioning during that time?

Yes, those wired and irritable phases have been coming and going for about a year and eight months, often lasting for days or even weeks, and they absolutely impair my daily life. During those times, I let bills pile up, miss appointments, and start countless projects only to leave them in messy, unfinished piles around the house. It also causes a lot of strain and constant arguments with my husband and kids because my mood gets so easily annoyed.

Can you confirm whether you have experienced at least one period of hypomanic symptoms, such as feeling extremely high or irritable, that lasted at least four consecutive days but less than two weeks, without a significant depressive episode immediately following it?

I'm really not sure about the exact number of days those high periods last or whether they are immediately followed by a low period. But I can definitely confirm that I have those high-energy phases on and off. It's just hard for me to track the exact timing and how they transition when I'm in the middle of it.

Can you think of any time when you felt extremely high or irritable for at least four consecutive days but less than two weeks, and during that time, did you experience any significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning that was noticeable to others?

Yes, I experience those wired, irritable phases for several days at a time, where I sleep very little, talk fast, and get easily annoyed over minor things. My family definitely notices because I rush around starting multiple projects, like reorganizing or gardening, only to leave them half-finished. This causes a lot of tension at home and makes it really hard for me to keep up with my normal responsibilities.

Yes, I definitely have those high, wired, and easily irritated phases that last for days at a time and have been coming and going for over a year and a half. A few months ago, I had a stretch of about five days where I only slept three hours a night, buzzing around reorganizing closets and planning art courses on my laptop.
